sourceRefs.locator: Section Rūs, paragraphs 74–78 and pp. 27–29. Merchants at the Itil, houses on the bank, enslaved women, sable pelts, offerings and hoped-for buyer. The translation indicates where Yāqūt’s quotations parallel the Mashhad recension.
The Journey of Ibn Fadlan, 921–922, map. Pages 25–26, The reading of the caliph’s letter, for the embassy’s arrival in May 922. The market on the Volga, p. 40.
Introduction and annotated translation of the Rūsiyyah passage. The identification of the group seen by the envoy allows more than one interpretation.
Component 981-001, N54°58′44″ E49°03′23″. A regional point on the middle Volga. The archaeological site gives geographic orientation only.
UNESCO component 981-001, Bolgar. For orientation on the middle Volga. No specific wharf is identified in the text.
